newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary FX futures inactive on busy grains trade.
newsitem.headline: Hungary FX futures inactive on busy grains trade.

text.p: Hungary's foreign currency futures saw very low turnover on Wednesday due to a flat spot market and an active grains futures market, which attracted funds, a Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) source said.

The total turnover of foreign currency futures was 780 million forints on the BCE, compared with 4.85 billion forints on Tuesday, while foreign currency futures remained untraded on the Budapest Stock Exchange.
On the BCE the mark was in focus, accounting for 40 percent of the total 5,482 lots traded.
Half of the turnover in marks represented September basket deals with the dollar.

Basket deals are seen as a means of hedging against future large fluctuations of the dollar/mark and are based on the central bank's currency basket against which the forint is devalued by 1.1 percent per month.
The forint floats against a currency basket made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the Ecu.
September mark rose by 0.15 forints to 112.15, while dollar futures for the same month dropped 0.5 forints to 191.40.
The yen remained steady at 162 forints to 100 units for the December maturity, while September yen ros 0.1 forints to 155.65.
The central bank quoted the three currencies in its midday fix at 104.81 forints to the mark, up 0.14, 180.77 to the dollar, down 0.28 and 143.43 per 100 yen, down 0.19.
